narrative:
The 2020 San Francisco Giants entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season with modest expectations, and the team largely delivered exactly that — a 29-31 record that fell just short of the expanded playoff field. Yet within that modest ledger lived genuine drama, unlikely heroes, and moments of real brilliance that made the season worth watching.

The Giants came out of the gate with genuine electricity. In the final days of July, Donovan Solano and Mike Yastrzemski authored back-to-back monster home runs on the same night, and Wilmer Flores added a three-run shot two days later. It felt, briefly, like San Francisco might be a surprise contender. August brought more of the same early on, with Mauricio Dubón delivering a clutch three-run homer to keep the momentum alive.

But August turned dark quickly, and the culprit had a name: Trevor Gott. The reliever surrendered three catastrophic home runs in the span of nine days — to AJ Pollock, Mark Canha, and Tommy La Stella — each more damaging than the last, the worst costing the team 0.821 win probability in a single swing. The bullpen's fragility was exposed, and a winning record slipped away. Yet the Giants refused to fold. August 25th became one of the most thrilling single days of the season, with Belt, Dubón, Longoria, and Solano combining for a remarkable late-game rally against the Dodgers.

September told the story of a team that was just good enough to stay relevant and just flawed enough to miss out. Killer double plays snuffed out rallies, and Sam Coonrod's late-game implosion on September 25th — surrendering a three-run homer to Trent Grisham — symbolized how thin the margin for error was all year. Wilmer Flores provided one last jolt of joy that same day with an 11th home run, but it wasn't enough. The 2020 Giants finished two games under .500, watching the playoffs from home — a frustrating, fascinating, utterly 2020 kind of season.
